[USER] User expresses skepticism about the need to worry about acid rain and questions its significance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acid rain is a form of precipitation that contains elevated levels of acidic compounds such as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acid rain increases the acidity of lakes, rivers, and streams, affecting the health of aquatic organisms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acid rain can be toxic to many species of fish, insects, and other aquatic life, leading to declines in populations and disruptions of food chains.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acid rain can damage trees and other plants, making them more susceptible to disease and insect infestations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acid rain can affect soil pH, reducing soil fertility and leading to nutrient deficiencies in plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Measures taken to reduce the environmental impact of acid rain include emissions controls, acid rain monitoring, restoration projects, and education and outreach.
